name: Blind Hughie
description: Blind Hughie is a lighthearted domino variant where players must match tiles without knowing what they hold. Each participant keeps their tiles in a face-down row and can only flip the rightmost tile on their turn. If it matches the central line, it is played; otherwise, it is returned face-down to the left end of the row. It is a game of high luck and social energy, where a sharp memory provides the only strategic edge as tiles cycle back through the player's row.

history.origins: Originating as a casual variation of the standard Block domino game, Blind Hughie was developed to simplify the strategy and increase the element of surprise. It is a traditional Western folk game with long-standing popularity in English-speaking card rooms and Dutch cafes (where it is known as Billitonnen).
timeline: 19th Century: Variations of 'Blind' dominoes appear in European gaming records.
1950s: Standardized as Blind Hughie in popular American and British domino books.
Present: Remains a favorite introductory game for children and a casual 'wind-down' game for experienced players.
history.cultural: Valued for its ability to level the playing field between experienced players and novices, emphasizing fun and memory over complex calculation.
history.evolution: The game essentially removes hand-management from the Block domino engine, replacing it with a sequential memory mechanic.

setup.dealing: Players draw tiles based on player count (2p=7, 3p=5, 4p=5). Tiles are placed in a face-down row in front of each player. No one may look at their cards.

rules.objective: Be the first player to play all tiles from your face-down row.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Start**: A tile is turned from the boneyard to start the central line. 2. **Turn**: Flip over the RIGHTMOST face-down tile in your row. 3. **Match**: If the tile matches either open end of the line, you must play it. 4. **Cycle**: If the tile does not match, return it face-down to the LEFT end of your row. 5. **Boneyard**: Tiles in the boneyard are not used after the start.
keyRules: You must always flip the rightmost tile first.
Returned tiles must be placed at the opposite end of the row to preserve their cycle order.
The game ends when a player goes domino or the line is blocked.

strategy.basic: Concentrate on remembering the tiles you've returned to the row. When those tiles cycle back to the right, you will know exactly what you hold.
strategy.intermediate: Opponent Memory: Watch what tiles your opponents flip and return. If you know an opponent has a 6-4 at the end of their row, try to keep the line ends away from 6 or 4 to block them.
strategy.advanced: End-Line Control: If you know your upcoming tile is a double, try to play your current tile on an end that makes the other end match your double, maximizing your chance of a double-play next turn.
tips: Memory is the only skill—don't lose focus when tiles are being returned face-down.
Speed up the game by handling your row cycles efficiently.

variations.name: Billitonnen
variations.description: The Dutch variant where the leftmost tile is flipped instead of the rightmost.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Sources describe Billitonnen as using the same basic rules as Blind Hughie, with only the flip position changed.

scoring.description: Winner scores sum of losers' pip totals minus their own remaining pips. Game to 100 (2-player) or 61 (3-4 player).
scoring.winCondition: Emptying the player's row or having the fewest pips at a block.

synthesis.shortDescription: A luck-heavy domino variant where your tiles sit face-down in a row. Flip the rightmost tile — play it if you can, cycle it to the left if you can't. Memory gives a surprising edge in this deceptively simple game.
